The analysis focuses on the long-time behavior of correlation functions in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model.
The analysis specifically addresses how soft reparameterization modes affect correlation functions in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model in the infrared regime.
The authors map the effective action of the reparameterization Goldstone modes (soft modes) onto the action of Liouville quantum mechanics (quantum mechanics in an exponential potential).
The authors introduce a variable transform $f'(τ) = e^{φ(τ)}$.
The variable transform $f'(τ) = e^{φ(τ)}$ converts the non-local soft-mode action into a quadratic form.
The conversion of the non-local soft-mode action into a quadratic form allows for exact functional integration over the $\phi$-fields.
The exact functional integration over the $\phi$-fields uses spectral decomposition.
The exact functional integration over the $\phi$-fields uses modified Bessel functions.
The theoretical predictions for the Matsubara Green function $G(\epsilon)$ were compared against numerical results.
The numerical results were obtained through exact diagonalization of a system with $N=24$ Majorana fermions.
The numerical results were obtained for a fixed realization of disorder.
All zero-temperature correlation functions exhibit a universal decay proportional to $\tau^{-3/2}$ for times larger than the inverse single particle level spacing ($\tau \gg N \ln N$).
For the single particle Green function, the universal decay manifests as a zero-bias anomaly.
For the single particle Green function, the zero-bias anomaly has an energy scaling of $\epsilon^{1/2}$.
The study finds that connected $2p$-point correlation functions scale as $\langle G^p_{\tau,0} \rangle \propto M^{(3-p)/2}|\tau|^{3/2}$ at long times.
Exact diagonalization supports the findings that connected $2p$-point correlation functions scale as $\langle G^p_{\tau,0} \rangle \propto M^{(3-p)/2}|\tau|^{3/2}$ at long times.
Finite size effects with $N=24$ make resolving the precise $\epsilon^{1/2}$ exponent difficult at very low energies.
The agreement with analytical scaling at the smallest energies is imperfect.
The behavior at the smallest energies is influenced by the finite many-body level spacing.
The finite many-body level spacing exceeds the resolution of the current theory for $N=24$.
Exploring how these infrared universals reflect in manifestations of a holographic correspondence.
Demonstrated that proper inclusion of soft reparameterization modes reduces SYK long-time behavior to Liouville quantum mechanics.
